Chapter 10: The Practice of Returning to Love
You know, the journey we've been talking about isn’t just a one-time thing. It’s something you practice, day after day. Life’s always going to throw challenges at you—moments of fear, or times when you have to make a choice between fear and love. And honestly, your mind will wander. Old habits might sneak back in. The urge to fall back on fear? It never totally disappears.
But here's the good news: every day is a fresh start. Every moment gives you a new chance to come back to love.
Think about a retiree looking back on a lifetime filled with both happiness and regret. She finds herself worrying about the future—her own health, her family, even the kind of world her grandkids will grow up in. Some days, that fear feels huge. But over the years, she’s learned to pause, take a breath, and remember—love is always there for her. So, she writes letters to her grandchildren—sharing stories, encouragement, and hope. And as she does, she finds a deep sense of peace.
Returning to love is simple, but that doesn’t mean it’s easy. It really comes down to noticing when fear has crept in, and then gently turning your attention back to love. It means letting yourself off the hook for mistakes, showing kindness to others, and trusting that—no matter what—love is the most solid ground you’ll ever have.
There are so many ways to build this practice. Meditation, prayer, journaling, or just doing something kind for someone else—these all help. But the real heart of it is intention. Are you willing to choose love, over and over, even when it’s hard?
Picture a single parent, balancing work and family, feeling stretched to the limit. Some days, patience wears thin. Tempers flare. Exhaustion takes over. But she’s learned to forgive herself, to start again each morning, and to look for those little moments of connection and joy. Is it perfect? Not at all. But it’s enough.
Most people find that the more they practice returning to love, the easier it gets. The mind reacts less, the heart opens up more. Life stops feeling like a constant struggle and starts to feel more like a dance.
So here’s the invitation: let love be your daily habit. Bring it into what you think, what you say, and what you do. When you do that, your journey isn’t just about returning to love—it becomes your whole way of living.
